methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series D → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.5x) to $6.0B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Redwood Materials, a Series D climate and energy company founded by J.B. Straubel, is evaluated against a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company operating in the frontier energy and materials space. The target's last post-money valuation stands at $6.0B against $2.125B in total capital raised.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, applying a 1.5x multiplier typical for Series D advancement to the $6.0B base valuation, implies $9.0B. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector comparable-stage companies—KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C)—yields a median of $1.0B, though the peer range spans $700M to $3.0B, substantially below the target's current mark.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $850M (floor) to $10.3B (ceiling), with a median of $5.0B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty regarding whether Redwood's commercial advancement and market position relative to peers justify a premium valuation, or whether the peer set systematically undervalues the sector. The stage-progression method anchors closer to the company's stated valuation; peer comparables suggest potential overvaluation but may not fully account for Redwood's operational differentiation or capital intensity relative to named peers. Resolution of this tension requires further diligence on unit economics and commercialization timeline.
